/SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Issued at 231 PM MST Thu Nov 26 2026

An active and dynamic day is expected across the area on Saturday as 
a quick hitting storm system sweeps through the region. The synoptic 
setup will be driven by a potent upper level shortwave riding along 
the strong upper level jet stream. This will be carrying with it a 
sharp surface cold front which will drive major weather changes 
through the area on Saturday. The main change with today's update is 
a considerable acceleration in the timing of the frontal passage. 
Most of the latest suite of model guidance has the frontal boundary 
fully through the area by 10-11AM on Saturday (with the notable 
exception of the RRFS). A morning passage will mean that we won't 
quite see as distinct of a temperature drop, but expect a fairly 
sudden wind shift and small temperature drop, but this will really 
hold down Saturday's high temperature forecast. If the front indeed 
passes through in the morning hours, most areas will not exceed 40 
degrees on Saturday. Behind the front, expect winds to remain strong 
and gusty, but the threat for high winds will evaporate quickly 
after an hour or so behind the front. 

This system is also looking increasingly likely to bring the first 
widespread snow event of the season. Accumulation totals are not 
expected to be significant (outside of the mountains) due to the 
quick hitting nature of the event, but that doesn't necessarily mean 
no impacts. The primary lifting mechanism appears to be vorticity 
advection ahead of the shortwave trough axis, favorable jet streak 
dynamics (we are under the left exit region), and powerful 
frontogenesis sweeping through along the frontal boundary. In 
addition, models show very rapid surface pressure increases behind 
the front on the order of 2-4 mb per hour with some minimal 
convective instability thanks to steep lapse rates. The character 
appears likely to be banded snowfall, with locally heavy rates 
underneath, but it shouldn't last very long. Rates could be 1-2" per 
hour underneath the heaviest bands of snow, with some potential to 
reach snow squall criteria. Snow squall parameters are around 2 to 
4, largely limited by the weak instability. With the acceleration in 
the timing today, the primary period of concern actually now appears 
to be Saturday morning through the early or perhaps mid afternoon. 
Some snow shower activity should linger through the afternoon and 
into the early evening hours, as dry air will not be very abrupt to 
work into the area behind the system, but all activity should be 
done by the late evening hours. Most areas outside of the mountains 
should see around a dusting to an inch or so of snow, though the 
lowest elevations of the North Platte River Valley may not receive 
any. There is potential for amounts in the 1-3" range generally 
along the US-20 corridor and near Laramie where frontogenesis 
lingers for longer combined with favorable orographic lift into the 
Pine Ridge or southern Laramie Range.

Sunday will start off chilly as skies clear overnight behind 
Saturday's system. Despite more sunshine, we will still have a cold 
airmass in place, which should keep highs down in the upper 30s to 
lower 40s. The flow aloft will start to turn more zonal Sunday 
onwards, which will increase the potential for strong winds in the 
wind prone areas once again. 700-mb height gradients are marginally 
supportive for high winds in the Arlington/Elk Mountain area during 
the day on Sunday, spreading eastward to the Laramie range wind 
prone areas Sunday night into Monday as surface pressure falls east 
of the range. Current probabilities are around 60 to 70% for the 
Arlington area, and 50% for the I-80 Summit and Bordeaux areas. 
Elsewhere, westerly flow will resume warm air advection as 700-mb 
temperatures climb back above 0C Monday and remain there through at 
least Wednesday. This should push highs back to around 5-10F above 
seasonal averages. Conditions look largely dry, though there may be 
another round of light mountain snow around Monday into Tuesday with 
a weak shortwave passing through.
